item.title: Single-cell and network pharmacology study presented at IEEE BECITHCON 2026
item.description:
We are delighted to share that Musab Shahriar, Group Leader of In Silico Drug Discovery at CHIRAL Bangladesh, presented our collaborative research study at IEEE BECITHCON 2026 (IEEE International Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology for Health 2026).

The study, titled:

“Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Network Pharmacology Insights into the Therapeutic Potential of Withania somnifera-Derived Phytochemicals Against Cisplatin-Resistant Ovarian Cancer”

bridges single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) transcriptomics, computational biology, and network pharmacology to investigate cellular heterogeneity and chemoresistance mechanisms in ovarian cancer.

Key Highlights of the Study

  • Dissecting Chemoresistance: By leveraging single-cell transcriptomic profiles of ovarian cancer cohorts, the team mapped distinct cell states, transcriptional reprogramming, and critical molecular drivers associated with cisplatin resistance.
  • Natural Phytochemical Screening: The study systematically evaluated bioactive phytochemicals derived from Withania somnifera (Ashwagandha) through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and structural dynamics to identify high-affinity lead compounds capable of targeting resistance-associated signaling pathways.
  • Therapeutic Implications: Uncovering novel compound-target interactions provides computational evidence for natural product-derived adjuvant therapies to overcome drug resistance in high-grade ovarian carcinomas.

Research Team

This multi-scale investigation was conducted through the Big Bioinformatics Lab within CHIRAL Bangladesh’s Computational Biology division. Huge congratulations to the entire research team:

  • Sheikh Naem Islam Abhi
  • Musab Shahriar (Presenter & Group Leader)
  • Lamia Hasan Joarder Barsha
  • Mst. Afsana Meme
  • Md. Jubayer Hossain (Senior Supervisor & Founder)

item.title: Pan-cancer study of CCT5 published in Scientific Reports
item.description:
Our pan-cancer analysis of the chaperonin subunit CCT5 has been published in Scientific Reports.

The study examines CCT5 across 33 tumour types, covering gene and protein expression, DNA methylation, genetic alteration, immune cell infiltration, correlation with tumour mutational burden and microsatellite instability, drug sensitivity, and prognostic significance. CCT5 was overexpressed in most tumours and associated with poorer overall and disease-free survival in several of them; reduced promoter and N-shore methylation points to an epigenetic component, and amplification was the most common alteration observed.

The work was led by undergraduate researchers working through the centre’s supervision programme, from the initial question to the submitted manuscript.

item.title: Junior researcher intake is open
item.description:
We are accepting applications for the junior researcher track from university students in their first, second and third years.

The track is aimed at students who want to do research rather than read about it. Accepted applicants join one of our four groups, work under one-to-one supervision on an active project, and are expected to carry that project through to a manuscript. There is no fee, and there is no stipend.

No prior programming experience is required. Foundational training in Linux, R and Python is provided through the centre’s training programmes. What we do ask for is consistency — the projects run over months, not weeks.

Students from life sciences, computer science, medicine, public health, pharmacy, statistics, geography and environmental science are all a fit.
